title: VTube Studio vs Warudo: Which Fits Your Team in 2026?
description: VTube Studio animates Live2D models from a webcam; Warudo is 3D VTubing software with face and hand tracking and plugins. Compare tracking, scope and fit.
intro: VTube Studio animates 2D Live2D models using webcam tracking, while Warudo is 3D VTubing software with built-in face and hand tracking, custom 3D assets, a blueprint system and C# plugins. The first question is therefore which kind of avatar you own: a Live2D rig or a 3D model. This page compares scope, tracking, extensibility and documentation from the vendors' own pages, and notes that neither page we opened showed a price.
verdict: Streamers with a Live2D model should start with VTube Studio, since that is the format it is built around. Streamers or small production teams with a 3D avatar, who want hand tracking, scene assets and the option to script behavior, should look at Warudo. Price was not readable on either page, so check Steam and the Warudo site before planning a budget.
pick_a: Pick VTube Studio if your avatar is a Live2D model and you want webcam tracking in an app made for that format.
pick_b: Pick Warudo if your avatar is 3D and you want face and hand tracking, custom assets and room to extend it with blueprints or C# plugins.

text: VTube Studio is described by its developer as an app for Virtual YouTubers that makes it easy to bring your own Live2D models to life. The phrase your own matters: you bring a finished model, and the app drives it from your camera.
Warudo is described as flexible 3D VTubing software. A 3D avatar moves in a scene, so the software deals with assets, tracking and logic around the avatar, not just the avatar's face.
VTube Studio lists webcam tracking as a core feature. That suits a 2D rig where face movement is the main input, and a streamer with a modest PC.

Warudo lists built-in face and hand tracking, and also names Twitch and YouTube integration. Hand tracking adds an input that 2D face-driven rigs rarely use, and the integration points toward stream-driven reactions. We could not verify how well either tracks, since neither page published accuracy data.

Warudo's homepage names a blueprint system and C# plugins. Those are two levels: blueprints for people who want logic without writing code, plugins for those who do. A production team that wants a model to react to chat or donations has a path to build that.

VTube Studio links to documentation and keeps an API development page on GitHub, which indicates a way for other programs to talk to it. The text we read on that page was mostly GitHub navigation, so details are not confirmed here.
VTube Studio's homepage links to a Steam page for getting the app, and its listed platform is Windows. The text we extracted showed no price, so look at Steam.

Warudo's homepage and pricing URL gave no readable price either. Its handbook is available in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Spanish, which helps international teams. Budget time as well as money: a 3D scene with plugins asks more of a newcomer than loading a 2D model.

A solo streamer with a commissioned Live2D model gets the quickest start from VTube Studio. A studio producing a virtual host, with a 3D character and scripted reactions, has more to gain from Warudo.

If you are still deciding on the model itself, read [best VTuber software](/software/best-vtuber-software) alongside the model tools category, because the avatar format limits which software you can use.

faqs.q: Does VTube Studio work with 3D models?
faqs.a: Its official description centers on Live2D models, so it is built for 2D avatars. If your avatar is 3D, Warudo is the one described as 3D VTubing software.
Yes, its homepage lists built-in face and hand tracking.

faqs.q: Can I script behavior in Warudo?
faqs.a: The homepage mentions a blueprint system and C# plugins, so both visual logic and code are offered.

faqs.q: Where do I get VTube Studio?
faqs.a: The official site links to a Steam page, and the listed platform is Windows.

faqs.q: Are there docs in other languages?
faqs.a: The Warudo handbook is available in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Spanish.
